Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the chase. Suryakumar Yadav leads his troops out to the middle. It will be the left-hand, right-hand combination of Quinton de Kock and Reeza Hendricks to open the innings for South Africa. Arshdeep Singh has the new ball in hand. Arshdeep to de Kock. Two slips await. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, a stiff challenge awaits South Africa, but they do bat deep and the wicket has been a good one for batting. They will be looking for the kind of start India enjoyed in the Powerplay to get themselves going. The Indian bowlers have the advantage of seeing which lengths and pace worked for South Africa and will look to replicate that. Pace off was tough to hit, but if the dew arrives, the ball could slide onto the bat instead of gripping the surface. Back in a bit for the chase.

The Proteas found an opening after removing Samson and enjoyed a brief quiet period, largely through George Linde, but it didn’t last long. India were 115 after 12 overs, but the final eight overs produced 116 runs as the hosts got up to 231. That charge was driven by a 44-ball 105-run partnership between Hardik Pandya and Tilak Varma, with Hardik bringing up the second-fastest fifty for India, reaching the milestone in just 16 balls. George Linde conceded 19 runs in his first three overs before going for 27 in his final over. Lungi Ngidi may not have the wickets to show for his effort, but his off-cutters made it tough for the Indian batters to get him away.

A strong finish for India, with a 17-run over to close the innings. Lungi Ngidi and Marco Jansen had done a decent job before that, but Ottneil Baartman couldn’t quite nail the final over, and that surge has propelled the hosts to 231. It was a tough outing for South Africa in challenging conditions. After opting to bowl first, the South African quicks were all over the place with their lines and lengths early on, and the Indian openers made them pay. Sanju Samson, in particular, got off the blocks quickly and batted as though he had never been out of the side. Tilak Varma was quick to find his rhythm and ensured the momentum stayed firmly with the hosts even after losing Abhishek Sharma.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! South Africa will be relieved to have seen the back of Sanju Samson. Even after dismissing Abhishek Sharma, they were unable to stem the flow of runs, but will hope to do so now by bowling as many balls as possible to the new batter. On this surface, the quicker you bowl, the quicker it comes off the blade. The odd ball has held up when bowled slower through the air, and that will be the blueprint not just for the spinners but also for the quicks, with their variations becoming crucial at the death. India have the platform set, and with plenty of batting still to come, they will ideally want to push past 200. Suryakumar Yadav joins Tilak Varma out in the centre.

OUT! TIMBER! Beautifully bowled by George Linde and Sanju Samson has been bamboozled here. Linde gives this one a bit more air, drifting into the leg stump. The ball dips and lands before turning away sharply from the right-hander. Samson clears the front leg and looks to play for the line but the ball goes past the outside edge and crashes into the middle stump. Samson departs for 37 (22) and Linde gets the crucial breakthrough for his side.

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! Tossed up down the leg side, Varma looks to sweep but misses and the ball goes through the keeper's gloves as well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.4: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: A bit straighter now, fired in towards middle, Varma blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.3: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Pushed through a bit quicker and sliding it down leg, Tilak Varma tickles it fine and the ball races away into the fine leg fence.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.2: Donovan Ferreira to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Floated up on the pads, bowled from around the wicket. Samson sits down to sweep but gets it off the pads to short fine leg and collects a leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 6.1: Donovan Ferreira to Sanju Samson, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Varma looks to repeat the trick but misses and India end the Powerplay at 67/1! Slight adjustment from Bosch, bowling it a few inches shorter and slightly closer to the off stump. Varma gives the charge and looks to go over the off side but is beaten.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Corbin Bosch to Tilak Varma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! How's that for intent on the first ball? Length ball, pushed across off, Tilak Varma is quick to charge down the track and he stays leg side of the ball, hammering it through covers for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Corbin Bosch to Tilak Varma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tilak Varma is in at number 3.

OUT! CAUGHT! Strangled down the leg side, but Abhishek Sharma has reviewed it right away. A proper short ball from Corbin Bosch but angles it down the leg side. Sharma looks to pull it behind square leg but misses and seems to have gotten a feather through to the keeper. Quinton de Kock pouches it safely and the umpire raises his finger almost instantly. However, the third umpire is now called in and this looks very close on the first replay. UltraEdge rolls and there is a spike when the ball is next to the gloves and it remains OUT. Sharma walks back for 34 (21) and India lose their first wicket at 63.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Corbin Bosch
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, OUT! c Quinton de Kock b Corbin Bosch.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! High and handsome! Good-length delivery around off, Abhishek Sharma simply clears the front leg and lofts it on the rise, nailing it over long off for his first six of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Wide! On a hard length and pushed well across the left-hander, ends up spraying beyond the tramline and a wide is called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on middle and leg, Sharma gets cramped for room and pushes it down to the left of mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Swing and a miss! Bosch hammers a shorter length and angles it across off, Abhishek Sharma shimmies down the track whilst making room and looks to smack it through covers but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Corbin Bosch to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Corbin Bosch comes in to bowl the final over of the Powerplay.

Jansen bends his back and bashes the deck hard, over middle. Abhishek Sharma backs away and looks to flat bat it down the ground. Ends up bunting it down the deck and the bounce takes the ball over the bowler's head for a single. 15 runs off the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Finesse this time! Not a lot wrong with this ball, on a back of a length, in and around the off pole. Sharma waits on it and steers it with an open bat face between short third and backward point for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! 50 up for India! Full and slanted in from over the wicket, on middle. Abhishek shimmies down the track and stays leg side of the ball to get his hands through. With a still head, he launches it over mid off for a four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: On a hard length, on top of off, dabbed down to deep backward point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Jansen pushes one across the right-hander, on a length. Samson extends his hands into the lofted drive and goes over extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! Angled into the pads, on a length, Abhishek is beaten on the flick and a leg bye is taken as the ball drops on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Marco Jansen switches ends now. He went for 19 in his first over.

FOUR! Fortuitous boundary for Samson! Full and wide on off, Samson reaches out for the drive with his hands but gets an outside edge. Reeza Hendricks at slip flies to his right while Lungi Ngidi at short third flings himself to his left but the ball goes right between them.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely bowled! Baartman spots Samson back away and he follows him with a searing yorker, right at the toes. Sanju digs it out beside the strip on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...but safe! Baartman hits the hard length, on middle. Sanju backs away to go inside out but is hurried and the ball gets big on him. The bat turns a bit in his hand and it is sliced over and wide of the man at mid off to his left. Two runs taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Samson takes the aerial route this time! In the slot from Baartman, around off, Sanju meets the ball with a straight bat again and plays the lofted drive to the left of mid on for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls the length back slightly and it is in the corridor of off, Sanju attempts the drive through the off side but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Class written all over it! Full and at the sticks, Samson presents the full face of the bat and creams the drive down the track. The ball goes past the stumps at the bowling end and it races away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Ottneil Baartman to Sanju Samson, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: An early bowling change as Ottneil Baartman comes in to replace Marco Jansen.
Pitched up, on off, at pace, Sharma firms the drive along the ground to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: It seems like Quinton de Kock has taken one too many blows to the ginger fingers on the right hand and finally, the physio rushes out to have a look. The middle finger seems to be the major concern and by the looks of it, QDK might have already broken it on the very first ball of the innings, because of which, every sort of awkward take is causing him so much pain. Hopefully, he can continue. Right then, the physio has weaved his magic and QDK is good to go again, which is great news.

Oh, dear! Quinton de Kock is seething in pain. Drags the length back but it is another off-cutter, on off. Abhishek does not pick the slower ball again. He heaves across the line but the ball drops on him and goes under the bat. Quinton collects it on the bounce and is in a lot of pain. Seems like the ball made an impact on the already bruised middle finger of his right hand, on which he copped a blow on the first ball of the game.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: And again! Another ball that dips and drops in the blockhole, outside off, Abhishek has a swipe across the line but is beaten all ends up due to the slowness of the delivery.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Well bowled! A nicely disguised off-cutter from Ngidi, going across the batter, Abhishek Sharma does not pick it all and is outfoxed completely. He looks to launch it down the ground but the ball drops on him and sneaks under the blade.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: The previous shot seems to have chipped the toe end of Sanju's blade and he wants a bat change but will have to wait till the over ends, it seems.
Full and angled in at the pads, Sanju gets the front pad out of the way and jams it out behind square on the leg side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lungi Ngidi to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Full and on off, Abhishek goes after it with hard hands and ekes out an inside edge that goes through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Effortless from Samson! This is on a length, swinging back in, on middle. Sanju does not try to overhit this one and just whips it with timing over wide long on for a six. 19 runs off Jansen's first over. That also brings up 1000 T20I runs for Samson, along with 8000 T20 runs as well!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Marco Jansen to Sanju Samson, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: On a back of a length, on off, Sharma glides it behind square on the off side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good comeback from Jansen! Angling in and then nipping away, on a hard length, over off, Abhishek charges down the track and looks to force it away but is beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that three boundaries in a row, two of which have gone not where Abhishek intended them to go. Fuller and outside off, Abhishek has a swipe at it again and gets a thickish outside edge that flies well over the head of the leaping Lungi Ngidi at short third for four more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Not convincing this time around! With an upright seam, this is on a good length, outside off. Sharma swings at it as he looks to carve it away once again. The ball comes right off the toe end of the blade and it is skied but in the vacant deep backward point region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Carved away! This is on a length, outside off, Abhishek gets the width to free his arms and he stays leg side before slicing it over backward point. It almost went the distance. The ball bounced just in front of the boundary cushions at deep backward point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Marco Jansen to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Marco Jansen will share the new ball with Lungi Ngidi for South Africa.

Tight single! Shaping back into the pads, on a good length, on middle. Abhishek looks to turn it away on the leg side with a closed bat face but the ball holds its line. The leading edge pops up before dribbling in front of mid off. The batters sneak in a quick single and Markram misses his shy at the bowling end.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed across the left-hander, on a good length, Abhishek stands tall and plays it on the up. The ball goes on the bounce to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Abhishek Sharma is up and running! Fuller and swinging back in, on middle and leg. Abhishek shimmies down the track and swings through the line. Thumps it back over the head of Samson at the non-striker's end for a four.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Lungi Ngidi to Abhishek Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Sanju Samson and India are underway! Short and wide on off, Samson throws his hands at it and the ball flies off the outer half. The ball drops on the bounce and wide of the deep backward point fielder. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Lungi Ngidi to Sanju Samson, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten again! Fuller in length, closer to the off pole, moving away in the air. Sanju goes for the drive away from his body and is beaten past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Lungi Ngidi to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Goes past the bat straight away! Shaping away, a bit wide, on a back of a length. Samson flashes but fails to connect. The ball keeps rising on its way to the keeper and Quinton de Kock cops a blow on the fingertips of his right hand while trying to gather the ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Lungi Ngidi to Sanju Samson, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the final bout of South Africa's all-format tour of India. The two umpires are already out in the middle and the Protea players also make their way out to the middle. Abhishek Sharma is reunited with Sanju Samson at the top of the order for India today. It will be Lungi Ngidi who will get the first bite at the new ball and he is raring to go. Let's play...

South Africa (Playing XI) - Quinton de Kock (WK), Reeza Hendricks, Aiden Markram (C), Dewald Brevis, David Miller (In for Tristan Stubbs), Donovan Ferreira, George Linde (In for Anrich Nortje), Marco Jansen, Corbin Bosch, Lungi Ngidi, Ottneil Baartman.

India (Playing XI) - Abhishek Sharma, Sanju Samson (In for Shubman Gill), Tilak Varma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Shivam Dube, Hardik Pandya, Jitesh Sharma (WK), Washington Sundar (In for Kuldeep Yadav), Arshdeep Singh, Jasprit Bumrah (In for Harshit Rana), Varun Chakaravarthy.

India's skipper, Suryakumar Yadav says they were looking to bat first as they don't expect the wicket to change much. Adds that he doesn’t expect dew to play a big role and says that they will look to put runs on the board and then defend the total. Suryakumar mentions that it already feels like a full house and calls it the most beautiful stadium, saying he hopes the team can put on a show. Shares that the focus is on taking as much as possible from this game and continuing to play fearless cricket. In terms of changes, he informs that Jasprit Bumrah comes in for Harshit Rana, while Washington Sundar replaces Kuldeep Yadav and Shubman Gill, who picked up a niggle in Lucknow, is replaced by Sanju Samson.

The South African skipper, Aiden Markram, says that they will bowl first and reckons that the wicket looks good and they are hoping for some dew later on. Adds that they are looking forward to the game today and they also have a few matches at this venue in the upcoming T20 World Cup. Further says that they want to level the series and want to finish on a positive note. Ends by saying that he doesn't quite remember what the combination was in the 3rd game but George Linde does come in for Anrich Nortje.
TOSS - Aiden Markram calls it correctly, and South Africa have elected to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Deep Dasgupta is inspecting the deck and has Pommie Mbangwa alongside him. Deep starts by saying that the square boundaries are 63 meters and 65 meters and it is a 71-meter hit down the ground from where he is standing. Pommie chimes in and says that it is a black soil wicket but it does look a bit on the dry side. Expects that there will be some turn for the spinners by just looking at it. Deep further adds that there are cracks in the surface but they aren't loose, so it might not actually turn much and there isn't much dew predicted either. Ends by saying that ideally one would want to chase but during the Indian Premier League, the teams batting first did win most of the matches.

The 2025 edition of the Indian Premier League revealed a clear trend at the Narendra Modi Stadium in night games, with 6 of the 7 matches won by the side batting first. However, considering the time of year and the likelihood of dew setting in, it will be intriguing to see what the captain winning the toss opts to do. Stay tuned for the toss and team sheets.

On the other hand, South Africa have more issues to address. The Proteas are still searching for their ideal combination, and time is running out, with just three more T20Is remaining after this match to fine-tune their plans ahead of the World Cup. What has emerged during the white-ball leg for the tourists is that whenever the top order has fired, it has gone a long way in shaping the result in their favour. From that perspective, it will be up to Quinton de Kock, Aiden Markram and Reeza Hendricks to make a telling contribution.

With 50 days to go until the T20 World Cup, India have a largely settled combination, with only a few finer details left to iron out. The Men in Blue are chasing what would be their 8th consecutive series win in this format. Despite a lean patch, Shubman Gill will arrive feeling confident at this venue, where he has scored four T20 hundreds and centuries in all three formats. There were reports of Gill missing the Lucknow game due to a foot injury, and it remains to be seen how he pulls up. On the bowling front, Jasprit Bumrah missed the Dharamsala game for personal reasons but rejoined the squad in Lucknow and is likely to feature tonight.

Hello one and all! The Test series saw South Africa complete a clean sweep, while the ODI leg belonged to India, who won it 2-1. We now arrive at the final match of the Proteas’ all-format tour of India, here in Ahmedabad, with the hosts holding a 2-1 lead in the T20I series. After the fourth T20I in Lucknow was abandoned due to excessive fog, South Africa can no longer win the series, but they will be keen to finish on level terms.
... MATCH DAY ...

All eyes turn to the Narendra Modi Stadium in Ahmedabad as India and South Africa gear up for the 5th and final T20I, with the hosts holding a 2-1 lead after three contrasting games and the fourth abandoned due to thick fog. The series so far has highlighted clear themes from both sides, India's bowlers setting the tone in their wins with early breakthroughs and disciplined spells, while South Africa struck back through powerful top-order batting and a pace attack that exposed India's death-overs execution. However, India's biggest concern heading into this decider is their batting form, with Suryakumar Yadav still searching for rhythm and Shubman Gill struggling to convert starts, opening up discussions around whether Sanju Samson could be brought in to add urgency and clarity to the top order to support Abhishek Sharma who has been superb since his debut in this format. Players like Hardik Pandya and Shivam Dube remain crucial in controlling the middle and death overs with the bat, while Tilak Varma's composure and ability to absorb pressure in the middle order could be vital on a big ground like Ahmedabad. Jasprit Bumrah, Arshdeep Singh, and Harshit Rana will again be key in applying pressure with the ball on a surface that offers true bounce. South Africa, meanwhile, have been keen on giving game time across the squad, but will still look towards their match-winners, with Quinton de Kock and Aiden Markram expected to anchor the batting, David Miller providing the finishing punch, and Dewald Brevis offering X-factor value with his fearless strokeplay in the middle overs, while their bowling attack led by Marco Jansen and Anrich Nortje, supported by smart variations from the spinners, will be tasked with striking early and controlling the death. With a series win at home on the line for India and South Africa pushing to level things and take momentum forward, this finale promises a high-intensity contest where form, selection calls, and execution in key moments will decide the outcome.
